decision: How should the new Personalization section (after How it works) show that two children in the same Grade 3 class get two different books, while it stays short on a phone?
invariants: Same copy: eyebrow Personalization, title 'Same class. Two different books.', the same lead, label and link
Same two sample children (Leah, Kai) and the same three lines each: Assessment, Learning style, Next book
Same two pages, built from the real question bank with fixed seeds (src/lib/sample-children.ts)
Warm look tokens, Section, SectionHeader, Knot, Rise
Placed right after How it works; viewports 1280 x 900 and 390 x 844; reduced motion

options.name: Two columns
options.bet: Two grey cards side by side, each with the child, the three lines and the full first page below
options.benefit: Most direct and the most page detail on desktop
options.cost: Longest: 1.92 screens on desktop, 1.85 on a phone (pages cropped to a peek)
options.risk: Adds the most length to a page that is already long (D-072)

options.name: Switch
options.bet: One child at a time, with a Leah / Kai switch; lines on the left, the page on the right
options.benefit: Shortest on a phone: 1.30 screens; 1.63 on desktop
options.cost: Needs a tap to see the second child; uses JavaScript
options.risk: The contrast is the message, and most visitors never tap, so they see one child and one book

options.name: Report table
options.bet: A report-card table: rows Assessment, Learning style, Next book, First page; one column per child
options.benefit: Compares line by line; both children on screen on a phone: 1.37 screens; matches the report look (D-087)
options.cost: 1.77 screens on desktop; on a phone the two pages are small cropped thumbnails
options.risk: Reads as a data table, less warm; phone text columns are narrow

options.name: Fork
options.bet: One shared start ('Grade 3, same school, same class, same free assessment.'), then the pencil line forks to two rows: the whole page as a thumbnail beside each child's lines
options.benefit: Shortest on desktop: 1.25 screens; both children without a tap on a phone: 1.44 screens; the whole page shows, not a crop; the fork reuses the pencil line
options.cost: Pages are small, so they read as pictures of a page, not as readable text
options.risk: The thumbnails may be too small to show that the problems are real

sample_report.what: The real ReportCard (readOnly) for Leah, computed by the real session, facts section and report model: Grade 3, BC, every regrouping question wrong. Result: working level grade 3, Number and operations Developing (3 of 5), the other areas Secure, facts 22 of 24 at 2.4 s. A sample note with 'Take free assessment' sits above the report. 2.8 screens on desktop, 3.9 on a phone.

measured: Section height / viewport height, from the screenshot script; no horizontal overflow in any option
known_gaps: Learning style: the intake questions after the assessment are planned but not built. Today nothing collects how a child likes to learn, so the 'Learning style' line describes a step we do not have yet.

The report shows areas, not skills: Leah's report says 'Number and operations: Developing', not 'regrouping'. The section's 'A gap in regrouping' is one level more detailed than the report it links to.
The read-only report ends with 'Next step: Start Leah's books' and no button; on a sample page this line reads oddly.
The report has no 'Leah's work' row: the sample has no drawings.
Sitemap and /llms.txt entries for /sample-report are left for the build stage.

selection.edits: Copy, tags and box text per D-096; Next book row removed; page zoom on tap; equal page heights; sample report at a Grade 2 working level with a Take free assessment button; sample-children line removed. Variants A-C and the prototype route are deleted in the build.
